title: Image Data Quality and Finite-Value Repair
prompt:
Implement `analyze_image_dataset(images)` for a sequence of real-valued NumPy arrays. This exercise is finite-value repair, not a denoising model. Classify any 2-D array as `gray`; for arrays with at least three dimensions, a final axis of length one is `gray` and a final axis of length three is `color`. All other shapes are `unknown`; do not infer a channel axis from a one-dimensional vector.

An array is noisy for this exercise if any element is NaN, positive infinity, or negative infinity. Return a mapping with `types` (one string per array), `noisy_indices` (ascending input indices), `noisy_rate` (fraction of arrays with invalid values, or 0.0 for an empty dataset), `cleaned` (one independent floating-point array copy per input), and `quality` (a mapping with integer `total` and `clean` counts).

In each cleaned array replace invalid values with that same array's mean over finite elements; if no finite elements exist, use zero. Keep finite entries unchanged, preserve shapes, and never mutate or alias input arrays, including already-clean inputs. The channel convention and finite-mean replacement are local practice choices; they are not a recovered original interview contract.

example.output: one gray image with finite cleaned pixels
example.reasoning: Per-image repair avoids using values from unrelated images.

background_note: General preparation exercise. A bounded Notion/source audit did not recover an original interview prompt for this exact local contract. The former unverified OpenAI tag has been removed; technical documentation supports the method, not an interview occurrence. NumPy isfinite identifies NaN and either infinity as invalid. The repair policy is a per-array imputation baseline; it neither detects visual corruption nor performs learned/photometric denoising. This is outside the core non-CV interview review list.
